canonical_statement: Every square-integrable martingale adapted to the augmented natural filtration of a Brownian motion admits representation, up to its initial value, as a stochastic integral of a predictable square-integrable process with respect to that Brownian motion.
domain_and_universes: A probability space Omega; continuous time t >= 0; a real Brownian motion W and real square-integrable martingale M on the augmented natural filtration of W; precise Lean universes and object model remain open.
quantifiers: real Brownian motion W with augmented natural filtration (F_t)
hypotheses: W is Brownian motion and (F_t) is its augmented natural filtration
M is adapted and a martingale relative to (F_t)
M_t is square-integrable (with the horizon convention still to be frozen)
conclusion: There exists a predictable process H, square-integrable on each applicable horizon, such that M_t = M_0 + integral_0^t H_s dW_s (with equality mode to be frozen).

alternate_encodings.target: terminal-variable representation X = E[X] + integral H dW on a fixed finite horizon
alternate_encodings.relationship: classically yields the martingale-process form by conditional expectation under suitable filtration and integrability assumptions
alternate_encodings.checked_witness: none; candidate transport deferred to statement phase

alternate_encodings.target: local-martingale representation with locally square-integrable integrand
alternate_encodings.relationship: stronger/different integrability profile, not interchangeable at intake

excluded_degenerate_cases: A general filtration merely carrying W is not in scope: the Brownian natural-filtration/generation hypothesis is essential. Multidimensional Brownian motion, local martingales, uniqueness of the integrand, and finite-terminal-variable formulations are not silently included.
